clue.text: See core ideas changing about Church

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for Church
changing tells us the letters of core ideas are to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch someone's central beliefs shift with regard to the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a bishop's district. 'changing' rearranges the fodder into ARDIOCESE, and 'about' wraps it round the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district under a bishop's authority; the chief one, led by an archbishop, has this longer name.

clue.text: Has a spin in posh car

definitions.meaning: something that has a spin turns over and over, as a ball does along the ground
the ...-Royce, a luxury car, is familiarly called by its first name

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a drive in an expensive car.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb tumbles or turns over fits the first sense; the short name of the Rolls-Royce fits the second.

clue.text: Opposed upright member supporting House

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it comes after

parts.note: a stile is an upright part of a door or window frame

explanation.surface: An MP standing against something, propping up the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts STILE below HO in the down light. 'Upright member' suggests a principled MP, but it is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against or antagonistic toward something is a synonym of this adjective.

clue.text: Possibly serve up inside pub restaurant

indicators.note: inside means the reversed word for serve goes into the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to serve someone is to aid them

explanation.surface: A suggestion to dish up food in a gastropub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for serve, and 'inside' places it within the pub word. 'Possibly' marks the answer as one example of a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain an Indian is everyday shorthand for a curry house, one kind of eating place.

clue.text: Do with females commonly embracing ultimately fanciable clots

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them

indicators.note: embracing means the word for females holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: gals is a colloquial, common word for girls or women

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of fanciable

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about chatting up women, ending with an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of fanciable, which 'embracing' puts inside the slang for women. 'clots' looks like a noun meaning fools but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When blood or a sauce clots it thickens and sets, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: They pursue limits of knowledge kept by prophets

indicators.note: kept by means the chosen letters are held inside the word for prophets

parts.note: seers are prophets who see the future

indicators.note: limits of picks the first and last letters of knowledge

explanation.surface: Seers who search the very edges of what can be known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' gives K and E, held inside SEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who go after or search for something are its hunters or searchers, one of whom has this name.

clue.text: Fire criminal lot hosting 'Blue Peter'?

indicators.note: hosting means the combined words take the flag in among themselves

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a ration is one's allotted portion, one's lot
the Blue Peter is a blue and white signal flag flown by a ship about to sail

explanation.surface: A gang setting light to a children's television show, Blue Peter being a long-running British one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' takes the flag into the middle of the charade. The question mark nods to the TV programme, but here it is the naval signal flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge, destructive blaze is the meaning of this word, a grander synonym of fire.

clue.text: Bishops and pawn touching rows

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
on can mean touching, resting against
tiffs are rows, quarrels

explanation.surface: A chess scene of bishops beside a pawn, plus some ranks of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests lines on a chessboard, but it means quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontiff is a bishop, especially the Pope, the chief bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Formation fighting his battles capturing soldiers

indicators.note: capturing means the jumbled letters take the word for soldiers inside
fighting suggests the letters of his battles are in turmoil and rearranged

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A military unit fighting its campaigns and taking prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' turns HIS BATTLES into ESTABLISHT; 'capturing' puts MEN inside, before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Forming or setting something up is the act of founding it, a sense of this noun.

clue.text: Overtly gazes, letting eyes settle initially

definitions.text: Overtly gazes, letting eyes settle initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding five words

explanation.surface: Someone stares openly, letting their eyes rest on a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the opening letters of the first five words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare openly and lingeringly, often lecherously, is the meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Almost put out admitting temper is reckless

indicators.note: admitting means the shortened word lets the next word in
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
anger is temper, rage

explanation.surface: Someone nearly losing their cool and behaving rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the final letter, leaving DOUS, and 'admitting' lets the temper word in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazardous, risky behaviour can be called both of these adjectives, close synonyms in loose use.

clue.text: Charm of a fine cat's dissipating

indicators.note: dissipating means the letters of a fine cat's scatter and regroup

explanation.surface: A lovely cat's appeal fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a noun but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate or enthral them, a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: Actor employed by sex trade

indicators.note: employed by means the letters are held within the words sex trade

explanation.surface: A performer working in the adult industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a minor actor hired to appear in crowd scenes without lines.

clue.text: Passages east of Florida Keys

indicators.note: east of, in an across clue, points to the rightmost letter, the last of Florida

parts.note: keys are low islands, isles

explanation.surface: Directions to the islands lying off the coast of Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florida Keys' reads as a single place, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Passageways between rows of seats in a church or theatre are walkways of this name.

clue.text: Quite conservative Queen wears dresses, husband follows

indicators.note: wears means the dresses go around the abbreviation for Queen

parts.note: saris are dresses worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: A rather traditional queen in fine gowns, her consort trailing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' means the dresses go round the Queen abbreviation, and 'follows' puts the husband letter last. Square is slang for old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Square is slang for old-fashioned or conventional, and the -ish ending softens it to rather so.

clue.text: Maximum load for schooner?

parts.note: a schooner is a sailing ship but also a large drinking glass for sherry or beer; its full measure is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about how much cargo a sailing ship can carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a drinking vessel holds when filled to the brim is its full measure.

clue.text: Supporter nearly getting more rowdy

indicators.note: nearly means the word for the supporter loses its final letter

parts.note: a brassiere is a supportive undergarment, a bra

explanation.surface: A fan becoming louder as the match goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a sports fan; it is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy means loud and brash, so the comparative is louder or more raucous.

clue.text: Boro' under Southgate clinching game

indicators.note: clinching means the words Boro' under Southgate hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Middlesbrough under manager Gareth Southgate winning a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Southgate managed Middlesbrough (Boro') before England. The answer is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a school bat-and-ball game, a specific example of a game.

clue.text: Estate seemed strangely to possess new interior

indicators.note: to possess means the jumbled letters hold the next piece
interior confirms the letter for new sits inside
strangely means the letters of seemed come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A country house that oddly seemed to have new decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns SEEMED into DEMESE; N goes inside after DEME.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is the land attached to a manor house, held by its owner: an estate.

clue.text: Doesn't eat going without last of fine banquets

indicators.note: going without here means going outside, so the word for not eating surrounds the letter

parts.note: someone who fasts doesn't eat

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of fine

explanation.surface: Someone abstaining from food and missing out on fine dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' reads as lacking, but means outside: FASTS goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish formal meals are banquets, and these are a common synonym.

clue.text: One puts up vicar after tea, essentially

indicators.note: after means the vicar's word follows the letter from tea
essentially picks the central letter, the essence, of tea

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman, much like a vicar

explanation.surface: A clergyman hosting after afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts up' suggests giving a guest a bed, but means builds or raises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who builds or raises structures, such as scaffolding, is called by this agent noun.

clue.text: Particles found around hip articulations

indicators.note: around means the word for particles goes round the word for hip

parts.note: jots are tiny amounts, particles
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Bits found near the hip bone in an anatomy lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks anatomical, but it means trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulations in anatomy are the places where bones meet and move, such as the knee.

clue.text: Cut digit catching front of remote drone

indicators.note: catching means the shortened word holds the next letter inside
cut means the word for digit loses its last letter

parts.note: a thumb is a digit

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of remote

explanation.surface: Someone injures a finger while flying a remote-controlled drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims the digit to THUM, and 'catching' takes in the front of remote. 'drone' looks like the aircraft but is a hum.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, steady humming or droning sound is a synonym of this word.

clue.text: English jumper in charge for vault

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the word for charge

parts.note: to storm is to charge, attack
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: An English athlete in charge of the pole vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' and 'vault' suggest athletics, or the British sense of jumper as a sweater; here it is a kangaroo, and vault is a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault can be a strongroom or cellar for keeping goods, which is a room for storage.

clue.text: Occasionally, cops also called into foreign port

indicators.note: occasionally means take only every other letter of cops, the even ones

parts.note: AKA stands for also known as, also called

explanation.surface: Police sometimes summoned to a harbour overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' gives O and S from cops.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese city is a major seaport, so it is an example of a port abroad.

clue.text: Bad smell over time produces neurosis

indicators.note: over signals turning the abbreviation for bad smell the other way round

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a session is a period of time

explanation.surface: A foul odour lingering long enough to cause anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses BO to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation that preoccupies the mind is classed as a neurotic disorder, a kind of neurosis.

clue.text: Fellow comprehends American author

indicators.note: comprehends means takes in, so the word for fellow holds the abbreviation

parts.note: a twin is a fellow, one of a matching pair

explanation.surface: A man who understands a writer from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' suggests a man; it is a matching partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, writer of Huckleberry Finn, is an example of an American writer.

clue.text: 'Earthly time slips' describing Einstein's first experiment

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the word for slips encircles the letter

parts.note: to err is to slip up

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Einstein's

parts.note: a trial is an experiment

explanation.surface: A title for a quote about Einstein's early test of time on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometry sense of drawing round: ERRS goes round E to make ERRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Earth rather than to space or heaven is the sense of this adjective.
